# An all-dimensional aligned-simplex midpoint volume credit

This is a sharp geometric inequality for actual compatible fibers. Its
middle-simplex hypothesis is explicit. No general mixed-integer depth or
center-selection theorem is asserted.

Fix d>=1. Let v_1,...,v_(d+1) span R^d, satisfy sum_i v_i=0, and form
a minimal positive circuit. Define the centroid-zero simplex

    T={x: v_i.x<=1 for i=1,...,d+1}.

For compact convex L put h_L(u)=max_{x in L}u.x. Write |.| for ordinary
d-dimensional Lebesgue volume, and set

    rho_d=|T intersect (-T)|/|T|.

This ratio depends only on d, since all centroid-zero simplices are
linearly equivalent. It is strictly positive.

## 1. The sharp geometric theorem

**Theorem.** Let A,B,K be d-dimensional convex bodies satisfying

    B subset T,
    (A+B)/2 subset K,
    K={x: v_i.x>=-t_i for every i}.

Assume every hyperplane v_i.x=-1 meets int A. Then

    |K| > |B|/rho_d.                                  (1)

The factor 1/rho_d is sharp as an infimum under these hypotheses.

### Lemma 1: symmetrization controls B by one scalar

Put

    m=(1/(d+1))sum_i h_B(-v_i).

Then m>0 and

    |B| <= |T intersect (-mT)|.                       (2)

**Proof.** The barycentric coordinates of T are

    lambda_i(x)=(1-v_i.x)/(d+1).

They sum to one, are nonnegative on T, and their simultaneous vertex
values show that every permutation of the coordinates is induced by a
unique invertible affine self-map of T. That map fixes the centroid 0,
so it is linear. Because it maps T onto itself, its determinant has
absolute value one. Denote this finite group by G.

Let B_* be the Minkowski average of gB over g in G. Each gB has the
same volume as B, so repeated ordinary Brunn--Minkowski gives
|B_*|>=|B|. All gB are contained in T; convexity gives B_* subset T.
The action permutes the normals -v_i transitively and equally often.
Addition of support functions therefore gives

    h_{B_*}(-v_i)=m for every i.

Hence B_* subset -mT, proving (2). For an interior point p of B,
h_B(-v_i)>-v_i.p for each i; summing proves m>0. QED.

### Lemma 2: balanced opposite dilations maximize normalized intersection

For every m>0,

    |T intersect (-mT)|
       <= ((1+m)/2)^d |T intersect (-T)|.             (3)

**Proof.** For 0<t<1 put L_t=tT intersect (-(1-t)T). Convexity of
T gives

    (L_s+L_t)/2 subset L_((s+t)/2).

Indeed averaging a point in sT and a point in tT puts it in
((s+t)/2)T; averaging their memberships in -(1-s)T and -(1-t)T
gives the other required inclusion. Also L_(1-t)=-L_t, so those
two bodies have equal volume. Brunn--Minkowski at their midpoint
therefore gives

    |L_t|<=|L_(1/2)|.

Now take t=1/(1+m). Then

    L_t=(T intersect (-mT))/(1+m),
    L_(1/2)=(T intersect (-T))/2.

Scaling volumes proves (3). These intersections have nonempty interior
because 0 lies in int T and m>0. QED.

### Proof of the theorem

Put r=(sum_i t_i)/(d+1). There is a unique p in R^d satisfying
v_i.p=r-t_i for all i: the linear map x -> (v_i.x)_i has rank d
and image exactly the subspace whose coordinates sum to zero. Translation
by p turns the inequalities into v_i.(x-p)>=-r. If r<0 their sum is
inconsistent; if r=0 their sum forces every equality and hence x=p.
Since K is full-dimensional, r>0. Consequently

    K=p+r(-T),    r>0,
    |K|=r^d |T|,
    h_K(-v_i)=t_i.

Actual midpoint containment and properness of the A cuts give

    2t_i >= h_A(-v_i)+h_B(-v_i) > 1+h_B(-v_i).

Summing gives r>(1+m)/2. By Lemmas 1 and 2,

    |B| <= ((1+m)/2)^d |T intersect (-T)|
         < r^d rho_d |T|
          = rho_d |K|.

This proves (1).

To verify sharpness, for e>0 take

    B=T intersect (-T),
    A_e=(1+e)(-T),
    K_e=(1+e/2)(-T).

Every cut v_i.x=-1 is proper for A_e, and B subset -T gives
(A_e+B)/2 subset K_e. Moreover

    |K_e|/|B|=(1+e/2)^d/rho_d -> 1/rho_d.

This establishes the sharp infimum for the geometric theorem. It does
not assert global halfspace-depth criticality for this family. QED.

## 2. An explicit finite formula for the dimension constant

With the barycentric coordinates above, -mT imposes

    lambda_i <= (1+m)/(d+1) for every i.

Inclusion--exclusion on the standard simplex gives

    |T intersect (-mT)|/|T|
      =sum_(j=0)^(d+1) (-1)^j binom(d+1,j)
          [1-j(1+m)/(d+1)]_+^d.                     (4)

Here [s]_+=max(s,0); since d>=1, there is no 0^0 convention. For a
specified set of j barycentric coordinates exceeding c=(1+m)/(d+1),
subtract c from those coordinates. When 1-jc>0 the remaining simplex
is a translate of a simplex with linear ratio 1-jc, so its relative
volume is (1-jc)^d. When 1-jc<=0 its d-volume is zero. Boundaries have
zero d-volume, justifying either strict or weak inequalities in this
inclusion--exclusion calculation.

At m=1 this yields

    rho_d=sum_(j=0)^(d+1) (-1)^j binom(d+1,j)
                    [1-2j/(d+1)]_+^d.              (5)

In particular

    rho_1=1,
    rho_2=2/3,
    rho_3=1/2,
    rho_4=46/125,
    rho_5=22/81.

Thus the sharp midpoint volume factors in dimensions 2,3,4,5 are
3/2, 2, 125/46, 81/22, respectively. The planar theorem and its
conditional mixed-depth consequence are recorded separately in
`candidate cce182d75ffe5c52`.

## 3. A preliminary conditional mixed-depth margin

Write Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d and m_0=d+1. Consider actual full-dimensional
fibers A,K,B at -1,0,1 with no other nonempty integer fibers. Suppose
0 is interior to K, the geometric hypotheses above hold, and all m_0
ambient caps H_i={(z,x):v_i.x>=z} attain the actual raw mixed depth
Q of the source (0,0). No global depth-maximizer assumption is needed.
The comparison Q>=Gamma_d|K| is automatic: the middle traces cover K,
one contains its ordinary centroid, and each middle cap has volume at
most Q. Then, with M=|A|+|K|+|B|,

    Q/M > 3 Gamma_d/[1+2(d+1)Gamma_d+3 rho_d].        (6)

For d=1,2,3 this gives, respectively,

    Q/M > 1/4,
    Q/M > 4/17 > 2/9,
    Q/M > 81/376 > 27/128.

The last bound exceeds the d=3 target Gamma_3/2 by the factor 48/47.
The estimate (6) alone is weaker than the desired target at d=4.
Section 4 strengthens the cap profile and closes this explicitly
conditional regime in all dimensions.

**Proof.** Put a=|A|,k=|K|,b=|B|, and denote the A captured volumes
by U_i. Set u=min_i U_i and w=max_i U_i. Since the B captures are
zero, the middle cap volumes are Q-U_i. All these continuous-normal
caps are proper on K and have positive volume. Both the A traces
v_i.x>=-1 and the K traces v_i.x>=0 cover their entire ambient fiber.

The ordinary positive-part cover bound is

    |L|<=sum_i(c_i-alpha)_+ +alpha/Gamma_d            (7)

for every alpha>=0 when caps of volumes c_i cover a convex body L.
For clarity, it follows by successively removing from each cap a deeper
parallel cap until its retained volume is at most alpha. Each removal
is at most (c_i-alpha)_+, and all retained sets are convex. If zero
volume is reached the bound already follows; otherwise their final
centroid lies in a covering cap and ordinary Grünbaum bounds the final
body's volume by alpha/Gamma_d. Cap volumes depend continuously on
the parallel threshold, and their hyperplane boundaries have zero
d-volume, so the prescribed removals exist and closed caps cause no
loss. The complete argument is also Section 1 of
`candidate 64b80eee72258d21`.

Apply (7) to K with alpha=Q-w and to A with alpha=u. This gives

    k <= Q/Gamma_d-sum_i U_i+(m_0-1/Gamma_d)w,
    a <= sum_i U_i-(m_0-1/Gamma_d)u,
    a+k <= Q/Gamma_d+(m_0-1/Gamma_d)(w-u).           (8)

The coefficient m_0-1/Gamma_d is nonnegative: Bernoulli's inequality
gives (1-1/(d+1))^d>=1-d/(d+1)=1/(d+1).

Genuine criticality implies w<=2Q/3. Indeed fix the continuous normal
of a cap with A volume w and vary only its integer coefficient. Its
middle volume q=Q-w remains fixed. The endpoint captured volumes
vary continuously between (a,0) and (0,b), so at some coefficient
they are equal, say t,t. If t=0 then q>=t is immediate. If t>0,
both captured endpoint sets are convex bodies; actual midpoint
containment and ordinary Brunn--Minkowski give q>=t.
Depth criticality of the original cap gives q+w<=q+2t. Hence
w<=2t<=2q, as asserted. All the varied halfspaces contain the actual
source; this comparison uses genuine ambient depth, not a restricted
set of directions.

The geometric theorem gives b<rho_d k. The automatic middle comparison
gives k<=Q/Gamma_d. Consequently (8), u>=0, and w<=2Q/3 yield

    M < Q[rho_d/Gamma_d+1/Gamma_d
                       +(2/3)(m_0-1/Gamma_d)]
       = (Q/(3Gamma_d))[1+2m_0 Gamma_d+3rho_d],

which proves (6). The comparison Q>=Gamma_d k follows from the
middle trace cover, without comparing different mixed-integer candidate
points. Substitution of the exact constants
above gives the three displayed numerical fractions. In dimension
four, 2(d+1)Gamma_d+3rho_d=26/5>5, so (6) does not reach Gamma_d/2.
QED.

## 4. Top-three cap profiles close this conditional regime in every d

**Theorem (conditional all-dimensional mixed conclusion).** Under all
the actual three-fiber and depth-criticality hypotheses of Section 3,

    Q/M > Gamma_d/2                                 (9)

for every d>=1. More explicitly the proved bounds are

    Q/M > 1/4                         for d=1,
    Q/M > 4/17                        for d=2,
    Q/M > 81/376                      for d=3,
    Q/M > 768/3589                    for d=4,
    Q/M > Gamma_d/(5/3+rho_d)          for d>=5.

In the last line rho_d<1/3. All hypotheses of the geometric theorem
remain in force, especially the aligned-simplex middle fiber and every
proper A cut. The source must have genuine ambient critical caps;
equal cap masses or local stationarity do not replace that assumption.
The comparison Q>=Gamma_d k follows from their middle trace cover.

### 4.1. A uniform bound for the intersection constant

We prove

    rho_d<1/3 for every d>=5.                        (10)

Let n=d+1 and let (X_1,...,X_n) be uniformly distributed on the
standard barycentric simplex, so X_i>=0 and sum_i X_i=1. Equation
(5) expresses

    rho_d=P(X_i<=2/n for every i).

We first establish, for any c in [0,1],

    P(X_i<=c for every i)
        <= [1-(1-c)^(n-1)]^n.                      (11)

For any subset I of indices excluding i, the conditional probability

    g_I(x)=P(X_j<=c for all j in I | X_i=x)

is nondecreasing in x. Indeed, conditional on X_i=x<1, the remaining
vector has the form (1-x)Y, where Y is uniform on the lower-dimensional
barycentric simplex. This follows directly by the affine scaling of
each simplex slice. Thus g_I(x) is the probability of the increasing
threshold event Y_j<=c/(1-x) for all j in I. Its value at x=1 is
irrelevant to the continuous marginal distribution.

The function f(x)=1_{x<=c} is nonincreasing. For an independent copy
X_i' of X_i, opposite monotonicity gives

    2 Cov(f(X_i),g_I(X_i))
      =E[(f(X_i)-f(X_i'))(g_I(X_i)-g_I(X_i'))]<=0.

Consequently

    P(X_i<=c, X_j<=c for j in I)
      <=P(X_i<=c)P(X_j<=c for j in I).

Apply this successively to the original marginals and successively
smaller index subsets. All marginal probabilities are equal. The
simplex dilation X_i>c has relative volume (1-c)^(n-1), so iteration
proves (11). No independence of distinct barycentric coordinates is
assumed.

Set p_n=(1-2/n)^(n-1), for n>2. The function

    p(x)=(1-2/x)^(x-1),    x>2,

is increasing. To check the derivative, put y=x/(x-2)>1. Then

    (log p(x))'=-log y+(y-1/y)/2.

The right side, as a function of y, vanishes at y=1 and has derivative
(y-1)^2/(2y^2)>=0. It is therefore positive for y>1. Thus p_n>=p_4=1/8
for every integer n>=4. For n>=9, equation (11) gives

    rho_(n-1)<=(7/8)^n<=(7/8)^9<1/3,

where the last strict inequality is the integer comparison
3*7^9=121060821 < 134217728=8^9.

The remaining indices n=6,7,8 are evaluated exactly by (5):

    rho_5=22/81,
    rho_6=3364/16807,
    rho_7=151/1024.

Each is less than 1/3, proving (10).

### 4.2. The stronger ordinary cap profile

For d>=2 put

    kappa=1/Gamma_d-2.

Then 0<=kappa<1. Indeed
(1+1/d)^d>=2 by its first two binomial terms, while
(1+1/d)^d<=sum_(j=0)^d 1/j!<3. The last inequality follows, for
example, by comparing j! with 2^(j-1) for j>=2 in the infinite
series, with a strict inequality from j=3 onward.

For any covering family of at least three cap volumes sorted as
c_1<=...<=c_m, apply the positive-part bound (7) with
alpha=c_(m-2). Only the largest two exceed this threshold, so

    |L|<=c_m+c_(m-1)+kappa c_(m-2).                (12)

Tied cap volumes cause no change to this identity. Sort the actual A
volumes U_1<=...<=U_m, where m=d+1. Applying (12) to A and to the
middle cap volumes Q-U_i, whose order is reversed, gives

    a <= U_m+U_(m-1)+kappa U_(m-2),
    k <= Q/Gamma_d-U_1-U_2-kappa U_3.               (13)

Every U_i<=w<=2Q/3 by the genuine fixed-normal tilt equalization
already proved in Section 3. Also b<rho_d Q/Gamma_d by the sharp
geometric theorem and the automatic middle-cap comparison.

### 4.3. Exact dimensional cases

For d=1 the two middle traces partition K up to one point, while the
two A traces cover A. Thus a+k<=2Q. Here rho_1=1 and
b<k<=2Q, yielding M<4Q.

For d=2, the correction from adding (13) is
(1-kappa)(U_3-U_1)<= (1-kappa)2Q/3. Substituting
Gamma_2=4/9, kappa=1/4, rho_2=2/3 gives
M<(17/4)Q, so Q/M>4/17>2/9.

For d=3 the correction is

    (U_4-U_1)+(1-kappa)(U_3-U_2)
       <= (2-kappa)2Q/3.

With Gamma_3=27/64, kappa=10/27, rho_3=1/2 this gives
M<(376/81)Q. Hence Q/M>81/376, and
81/376-27/128=27/6016>0.

For d=4, m=5 and the kappa U_3 terms in (13) cancel exactly. Their
correction is U_5+U_4-U_1-U_2<=4Q/3. Therefore

    M/Q < (1+rho_4)/Gamma_4+4/3
          =3589/768.

The resulting bound 768/3589 exceeds Gamma_4/2=128/625; equivalently

    2-[1+rho_4+(4/3)Gamma_4]=161/1875>0.

For d>=5, bound the three positive terms in (13) by
(2+kappa)w=w/Gamma_d and discard the three nonpositive terms.
This gives

    a+k <= Q/Gamma_d+w/Gamma_d
          <=5Q/(3Gamma_d),
    M < (5/3+rho_d)Q/Gamma_d.

Equation (10) now proves the strict bound in (9). These estimates use
only actual finite fiber sums, not a projected continuous integral.
All candidates compared in the depth argument belong to the original
mixed-integer set. QED.

## 5. Necessary support-simplex deficits when K is arbitrary

Now retain the actual depth-critical cap configuration, but allow K to
be an arbitrary convex body. Define its aligned circumscribed simplex

    Kbar={x: v_i.x>=-h_K(-v_i) for every i}.

The normals form a full-rank positive circuit, so Kbar is a bounded
full-dimensional simplex containing K. The geometric theorem applies
to Kbar and gives |Kbar|>b/rho_d. The cap profiles and equalization
remain valid for the actual body K.

If Q<=Gamma_d M/2, the resulting necessary bounds are

    |K|/|Kbar| < 6/7                 for d=2,
    |K|/|Kbar| < 12/13               for d=3,
    |K|/|Kbar| < 690/851             for d=4,
    |K|/|Kbar| < 3rho_d <1           for d>=5.        (14)

To verify them, the profile estimates above have the form
a+k<=Q/Gamma_d+C_d Q, with

    C_2=1/2, C_3=88/81, C_4=4/3,
    C_d=2/(3Gamma_d) for d>=5.

The bad target and the automatic middle-cap comparison imply

    2Q/Gamma_d<=M<=b+Q/Gamma_d+C_d Q,
    k<=Q/Gamma_d<=b/(1-Gamma_d C_d).

Each displayed denominator is positive. Dividing by
|Kbar|>b/rho_d gives (14), with exact factors
rho_d/(1-Gamma_d C_d). These are restrictions on a hypothetical bad
configuration. A deficit from this prescribed support simplex by itself
does not imply an ordinary depth surplus: that simplex need not be a
minimum-volume enclosing simplex. No such inference is used here.

## Scope and transformations

Every body and every volume in this note is in the continuous fiber
space. The finite symmetrization is used only to prove the scalar
volume inequality; it is not substituted for the original mixed-integer
set or its chosen center. No integer coordinate is transformed. There
are no smoothness, rationality, or finite-facet hypotheses on A or B.
The simplex description of K is an explicit essential assumption of
the proved statement, not a conclusion about arbitrary critical fibers.
